title_original: You Can See Everything passes $100m at global box office as UK release starts strong
excerpt_original: The documentary from Nathan Fielder following fraudster Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks leading up to her imprisonment has broken box office records in the UK Elizabeth Holmes film You Can See Everything has crossed the $100m mark at the global box office as it recorded the…

blocks.text: Elizabeth Holmes film You Can See Everything has crossed the $100m mark at the global box office as it recorded the highest ever opening weekend figure for a non-music documentary in the UK.

Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything earned an estimated $2.5m over the weekend on its sixth week of release in North America, according to Box Office Mojo , bringing its total there to $93.5m. This has been augmented by successful releases in a number of international territories, which has added an estimated $9m for a total of $102.5m.

This means the film is already the seventh highest grossing documentary of all time, in a list currently headed by the 2009 film Michael Jackson’s This Is It on $267.9m. In North America alone, it is now the third highest grossing documentary, behind Fahrenheit 9/11 and Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour.

Despite releasing a month and a half later, the UK has seen stellar figures on the film’s first weekend in cinemas. Variety reports it took an estimated $3.2m (£2.4m) from more than 590 venues, itself a record for a non-music documentary.
You Can See Everything has proved to be a significant commercial success for its backers, which include distribution outfit A24, with the film reportedly costing $7m to make.
